summary: Scheduled SFTP delivery of daily cryptographically-signed audit archives + manifest for external financial audit
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a nightly delivery of Redwood audit logs for the previous day via customer-managed SFTP endpoint. Each delivery must include a compressed audit bundle (.tar.gz), a machine-readable manifest listing file-level SHA256 checksums, and a detached cryptographic signature (RSA-2048 or ECDSA P-256) over the manifest. This is to satisfy a scheduled third-party financial audit that requires end-to-end integrity evidence and transfer proof.

Impact:
- Compliance requirement for Q1 financial audit.
- Customer will not be able to complete auditor review until signed bundles are received for the audit window (2026-01-01 to 2026-03-31).

Requested delivery cadence and retention:
- Daily at 02:00 UTC (previous calendar day logs).
- Maintain 90 days of archived bundles available for re-delivery on request.

Functional requirements from customer:
1) Each bundle contains: audit-events.log (newline-delimited JSON), access-control.log, admin-audit.log (if present).
2) A manifest.txt with lines: <filename> <sha256_hex> <bytes>
3) A detached signature file manifest.sig created using a customer-accepted key algorithm (customer prefers RSA-2048 with PKCS#1 v1.5).
4) Transfer over SFTP with server-host-key verification and mandatory TLS client certificate auth (customer will provide client cert).
5) Option for PII redaction flag (customer will specify whether user_identifiers should be redacted; default deliver full logs unless redaction requested).
6) Delivery notification via HTTPS callback (webhook) to a customer URL with delivery metadata (filename, checksums, timestamp).

Acceptance criteria:
- Successful handshake and test upload to customer's SFTP endpoint with files matching manifest and valid signature.
- Delivery scheduled and automated in production for 7 consecutive nights without failures.
- Auditor can validate manifest checksums and verify detached signature against provided public key.

Validation steps for Support/Eng:
- Coordinate certificate and SFTP login with customer's security contact.
- Land proof-of-concept PR that generates signed manifest and performs SFTP push. See related_github_prs.
- Run end-to-end test with customer holding an auditor present if requested.

Notes:
- Customer asked whether Redwood can use HSM to sign manifests. They accept Redwood signing if we can provide evidence of key lifecycle controls. Action: confirm with Security whether HSM-backed signing is supported for customer artifacts or if we must support customer-supplied signing keys.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - configuration and delivery request. To reproduce transfer failure: attempt SFTP connection to customer's endpoint using provided client cert and validate manifest/signature chain.
logs: N/A - no runtime error logs; customer provided sample manifest in initial request. Production delivery logs will be stored in internal audit-delivery job runbook (Confluence link).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Priya Rao (Customer Support): Received request from customer security ops for scheduled signed bundles. Customer provided SFTP host, username, port, and public cert for server host-key. Asked for clarifications on signing algorithm and HSM usage.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Marco Diaz (Integrations Eng): Confirmed we can produce SHA256 checksums and generate detached signatures. Need Security to confirm whether we can sign with our HSM-backed key for customer artifacts or whether customer will sign on receipt. Opened quick RFC with Security.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Leah Patel (Security): HSM signing is available but requires an exception for exporting signed artifacts. Proposed two options: 1) Redwood sign and provide KMS evidence (keyid-redwood-signer-01) or 2) Redwood produce unsigned manifest and customer performs signature after transfer. Need legal approval for option 1.

2026-03-11 14:05 - Priya Rao (Customer Support): Shared both options with customer. Customer prefers Redwood-signed manifests to reduce auditor friction but is willing to accept customer-side signing if HSM evidence requires additional lead time.

2026-03-12 10:00 - Marco Diaz (Integrations Eng): Created a prototype job that bundles logs, computes SHA256 checksums, and produces a manifest.sig using RSA-2048. Uploaded test artifact to customer's staging SFTP and confirmed manifest verification with customer's security. Preparing PR for production automation. See related_github_prs.
2026-03-12 16:20 - Priya Rao (Customer Support): Scheduled a call with customer for 2026-03-13 to complete certificate handshake and run an end-to-end acceptance test.
resolution: Pending - prototype validated in staging. Next steps: Security/legal sign-off for HSM-backed signing or acceptance of customer-side signature, then schedule production rollout and monitoring.
